Six C include-reference projects retain complete canonical and supplementary observations from pinned Joern 4.0.555. Two source projects are new; four reuse exact historical sources. All six accepted Rust canonical outputs already matched the fresh references. The added assertions concern include metadata, not new canonical matches or complete Joern parity.

| Case | Source files | Observed import/dependency pairs |
|---|---:|---:|
| duplicate_supplied_macro_local | 3 | 2 |
| inactive_body_include | 2 | 2 |
| repeated_direct_include | 2 | 2 |
| tiny_fixedtables_include | 2 | 1 |
| tiny_fixedtables_inline | 1 | 0 |
| unresolved_include_pair | 1 | 2 |

Each case contains untouched input files, its complete canonical `expected.txt`, the complete `joern-supplement.jsonl`, and accepted Rust raw outputs, statuses and actual CPG2 version2 saved graph. The canonical batch retained all four historical full-byte anchors. Its raw stdout/stderr and exact scripts, release and admission receipt are in `provenance/canonical`. The separately admitted observer reopened copies of all six saved Joern graphs without parsing or applying default passes; its full raw output, scripts, release and receipt are in `provenance/observer`. Runtime inventories and original preparation are retained. Large original runtime binaries and saved Joern stores remain local at the hash-bound receipt paths; this package does not claim those paths exist in a fresh clone.

`derive-expected.py` mechanically creates each `expected-include-metadata.json` from the complete admitted supplement. Run it with `--verify` to reproduce and compare those bytes without overwriting anything. It retains every observed IMPORT and DEPENDENCY property, all incident edge occurrences and their namespace/import/dependency endpoints. Identical dependency property maps remain distinct through their individual import occurrences. No graph record is trimmed or deduplicated. Full original numeric classes and IDs remain in the raw supplement; derived assertions compare exact integer values in their stated domains, not fabricated Java classes on Rust values.

The production tests build the exact source sets through `Project`, `CFrontend` and the standard analysis pipeline. They compare all six complete canonical graphs and all observed include components, then save/load actual CPG2 version3 stores and repeat the metadata and canonical checks. IMPORT ORDER must be explicitly present; DEPENDENCY ORDER must be explicitly absent. Optional strings, lines and columns preserve absence. The owner’s physical file and global namespace full name are checked independently of cross-producer node IDs. Existing global TYPE_DECL dense ORDER values are checked separately, without inferring property presence for those legacy nodes.

All eighteen incident Joern edge payloads are null. Rust edge-payload storage remains unsupported; these tests compare every incident edge kind, endpoint and multiplicity, not payload storage. The full raw graphs retain other AST, dominance, dataflow, location and property differences. In particular, the external macro BINDING discrepancy in the repeated control is separately classified in `provenance/reviews/classification-addendum.json`; this family does not conceal or fix it.

The observed inventory includes inactive directives, repeated guarded includes and both unresolved quoted/system requests. Each pair belongs to the physical caller’s global namespace. These six controls do not establish general include search or macro-computed include-name behavior. Source implementation and final candidate validation are separate from this reference preparation; `measurement.json` records the preparation state, and later candidate receipts must identify their own exact sources and executables.
